text:
Maya: @here seeing a sudden cluster of OOMs 10:14 UTC on prod-dedicated. Kernel selector picked nvfuser on a subset of pods and workspace usage jumped ~1.8x compared to the baseline. KV cache also spiked for long-chat sessions. Example log snippet:
```
2026-03-16T10:14:02Z ERROR runtime: alloc failed: out of memory, workspace_needed=1.9GB, free=1.1GB, kernel=nvfuser_fused_attn
```
Maya: impact ~6 pods, ~30% request fail rate on that shard, retries causing latency increase. Need quick mitigation and then root cause.
Jun: which service/version? can we rollback canary instead of broad change?
Maya: svc/llm-runtime on dedicated-gpu-us-west-2, image runtime:v2026-03-17-nvfuse-canary. Canary is ~20% of traffic on that pool but we saw cross-pod packer combine causing large batch groups.
deploy_bot: Rollout triggered: rollback svc/llm-runtime image -> runtime:v2026-03-16-stable (initiated by Jun) :construction:
Sasha: quick profiling shows peak workspace ~1.9GB at batch=8. nvfuser allocs an extra temp buffer for block fusion; combined with KV cache per-session growth it pushes pods over headroom. Batch heuristic intentionally grouped by seq_len similarity — that's the trigger.
Sasha: proposed immediate mitigations: 1) clamp max_batch_size=4 for nvfuser-tagged kernels, 2) disable cross-batch fusion on those kernels, 3) apply allocator soft-headroom +10% for affected nodes.
Priya: agree. Also tighten KV cache soft cap on prod-dedicated: set session_kv_soft_limit=150MB and ttl_active=60s so inactive sessions are evicted sooner. Command to hotpatch config:
```bash
rdctl config set svc/llm-runtime session_kv_soft_limit=150MB session_kv_ttl=60s --target dedicated-gpu-us-west-2
```
Theo: add a request_shaper rule to route very long sequences to the quantized fallback model and reject >2048 tokens when under memory pressure. Sample policy: 
```json
{"when": {"total_tokens": ">2048"}, "action": "route", "target": "llm-runtime-quant-q4"}
```
Jun: can we avoid full rollback? maybe flip a per-node flag to disable buffer_reuse for just the affected hosts as a quicker mitigation. That should free ephemeral temp buffers at cost of some perf.
Maya: good call. Doing a hotpatch: set buffer_reuse=false on the 6 pods, and clamp max_batch_size=4.
RuntimeBot: Hotpatch applied to nodes [gpu-uw2-12, gpu-uw2-14, gpu-uw2-19, gpu-uw2-21, gpu-uw2-23, gpu-uw2-27]: buffer_reuse=false, max_batch_size=4. Monitoring CPU/GPU memory for 10m.
Maya: after patch, errors dropped to near-zero on patched nodes and overall fail rate decreased to <2%. Latency impact ~+6% p95 on those nodes. Rolling patch across remaining pool.
Priya: I'll open a runbook PR with immediate checklist: rollback if needed, hotpatch shaper, kv-ttl enforcement, disable buffer_reuse toggle, and circuit breaker thresholds. Add alert rule: kernel_workspace_ratio > 1.3 for any kernel variant.
Sasha: followups: add a regression test that replays long-chat traces (high KV retention + varied seq lengths) against nvfuser path and a perf test for batch packing behavior. Also add telemetry to kernel selector to weight workspace peak as a primary metric in selection heuristics.
Theo: I'll author the circuit policy change to route >1024 token high-memory requests to fallback quantized models and to reject >4096 outright during memory pressure windows. Policy will include a cooldown backoff.
Jun: owner sync: Priya -> runbook & incident timeline, Sasha -> regression test & selector metric, Theo -> circuit/routing policy, Maya -> full incident writeup and postmortem.
Maya: thanks all — will post timeline and attach heap/profile artifacts to the incident ticket. :heart:
